chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, raising it, who said:
"The sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding the ḥanūṭ is thirteen dirhams and one-third as its maximum."

And he said: "Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام descended to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with ḥanūṭ, and its weight was forty dirhams. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله divided it into three parts: one part for himself, one part for ʿAlī, and one part for Fāṭimah عليها السلام."

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the normative prophetic tradition or prescribed practice
key_terms.الْحَنُوطِ: the perfuming substance applied to the deceased in funeral preparation
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel who brought the ḥanūṭ
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a unit of weight used here to measure the ḥanūṭ
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ: Fāṭimah عليها السلام, recipient of one portion

ai.seo_question: What is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) amount of ḥanūṭ for the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the sunnah (prophetic tradition) amount for funeral ḥanūṭ and indicates that its upper amount is thirteen and one-third dirhams. It also narrates that Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام brought ḥanūṭ to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, who divided it into portions for himself, ʿAlī, and Fāṭimah عليها السلام.
